name: Super Sushi Samurai stale-balance self-transfer inflation
summary: SSS's custom _update() read the recipient balance before debiting the sender and then wrote it back plus the amount, so every self-transfer minted the amount. The first user self-transferred 272B SSS and sold it into the SSS/WETH pair; four days later a whitehat repeatedly doubled its balance and emptied the pair, and copycats inflated the pair via skim(pair).
notes: The first seller's 7.6T SSS were mostly genuine allocations collected from 28 wallets; only the WETH its self-minted 272B SSS added to the swap (marginal output at pre-swap reserves) is counted. The whitehat's 0.01 WETH setup buy (ref) is netted; its later return (ref) is a recovery and is not.

Campaign: every pair WETH withdrawal funded by self-minted SSS (first seller's sale, whitehat mint and cash-out, blackhat skim(pair) drain, seven c0ffeebabe repeats). A scan of all self-transfers to block 1.4M finds no other material sale (other self-transferers' pool withdrawals total under 0.6 WETH).
Router sells between the game players' first self-transfers and the whitehat drain may carry minted SSS passed on to other wallets; that provenance is not traced, so the loss is a floor.
